content.text: Base plate foundation, then tan walls with door and window.
Roof core beams plus two test slopes to check slope orientation.
Laying the dark-red roof: eave course and upper course of slopes.
The 1x2 slopes aren't rendering (missing mesh) and they landed facing the wrong way — swapping to 2x2 slopes.
The slope part has no mesh in my renderer, but it's real in the model. Removing the 21 misplaced slopes, then re-laying with 2x2 slopes.
Removing the two stray test slopes, then laying the roof with measured orientation.
The slopes landed half-stud off (the solver used tube-on-stud seatings). Clearing them and re-seating on exact wall studs.
Prototype slope is now exactly on the wall studs. Making it a module and stamping the eave course.
Level-2 slopes next — seating a prototype on the inner beam.
Window glass and a doorstep, then tying the structures together.
Glass brick landed on the roof — moving it into the window opening.
The window gap is two courses tall — fitting a real window frame.
